clue.text: Plans unfortunately covering only a little time

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps round the other, holding it inside

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
T is the standard abbreviation for time, a mere scrap of the word

explanation.surface: Someone's plans have gone awry and leave hardly any time to carry them out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts T inside ALAS. 'Plans' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: maps and charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps is a collection of charts or drawn plans of territory.

clue.text: A church's foremost religious job, being precise

indicators.note: foremost means the first letter of church is taken

parts.note: a curacy is the post of a curate, an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A church's leading clerical post requires exactness.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness or correctness is the state of getting things right.

clue.text: The coast? Absolutely exact, one hears

indicators.note: one hears tells us the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: literal means exactly as stated, word for word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the shoreline is a precise match.
explanation.walkthrough: LITERAL and LITTORAL are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, littoral means the shore region of a sea or lake.

clue.text: Commemorative message delivered by air?

parts.note: by air seems to mean airmail, but it means sung to a tune: a greeting for a birthday or anniversary performed in person

explanation.surface: A celebratory note sent by airmail.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting delivered by a messenger who sings it, often for a birthday, an occasion being marked.

clue.text: Feature of piano leads to piano and forte being fluid

indicators.note: fluid things change shape, so these letters flow into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, these seven letters join the shuffle
p is the musical notation for piano, meaning softly
f is the musical notation for forte, meaning loudly

explanation.surface: A music lesson explaining how a piano's dynamics shift between soft and loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being fluid' rearranges LEADSTO plus P and F. 'leads to' looks like a link phrase but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand or upright piano has a left pedal that softens the tone, one of the instrument's features.

clue.text: Second boat needed to get to island

parts.note: Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A traveller needs a second vessel to reach an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small Channel Island near Guernsey.

clue.text: High-quality steering not right — delicate adjustment required

parts.note: fine means of high quality

indicators.note: not here says the letter for right is dropped from the steering word

parts.note: turning a wheel is steering

explanation.surface: Superb steering is off to one side and needs subtle correction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from TURNING, leaving TUNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making very small tweaks to get something exactly right, as with a radio dial.

clue.text: Go out with her friend? Don't be ridiculous!

explanation.surface: Someone is told to date a woman's companion and replies in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: Cryptically, to pull is to attract or go out with someone, and her friend is the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic reading means to chat up her companion; the idiom is a retort meaning you must be joking.

clue.text: Fail to stop dangerous creature?

explanation.surface: A fearsome beast that will not halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag on is to continue tediously without ending; a fire-breathing mythical monster is a perilous beast.

clue.text: News update from us city trial

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a city in the US
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A report on a court case in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the country USA, not the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent report is the newest bulletin.

clue.text: How to deal with short ball? Get away!

definitions.text: How to deal with short ball?

explanation.surface: Cricket advice about a short-pitched delivery, followed by a shout to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a short ball outside off stump can be cut (a square-ish slashing stroke) and then the batsmen take a run.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricketing reading is a stroke followed by a dash between wickets; the idiom means to flee hastily before trouble arrives.

clue.text: Father, taken aback in interruption to service, jumped

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the tennis call

parts.note: a let is a tennis call when a serve clips the net and must be replayed

indicators.note: taken aback suggests something pushed backwards, so the word for father is read in reverse

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A father, startled when a tennis serve is halted, leapt up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns father round and 'in' sets him inside the tennis call. A let is called when a serve clips the net, so play is interrupted and the serve retaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang into the air, the past tense of leap.

clue.text: Man that is an untrained soldier

parts.note: in chess the pieces are called men, and a rook is one of them
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone points out a man and says he is a raw recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw recruit fresh to the army is a novice soldier, slang term.

clue.text: Sick, so isn't at places of work

indicators.note: sick here means unwell or disordered, telling us the letters are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Someone is ill, so they are not at their workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick' rearranges SOISNTAT; the apostrophe in isn't is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or assigned spot where someone is placed for duty, as soldiers or staff are posted.

clue.text: Text on card game getting some oral attention

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the second word below the first

parts.note: bridge is a card game
a work is a written text, as in a literary work

explanation.surface: A rulebook about a card game receiving spoken comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral' means of the mouth: dental bridges and crowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental bridges fitted by a dentist are care given to the mouth.

clue.text: Campanologist in church infuriating the queen

parts.note: angering means making furious
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the queen

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer in church is annoying the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A change ringer rings church bells in mathematical sequences called changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanology is the art of bell-ringing, and one ringing changes on tower bells practises it.

clue.text: Mathematical quantity transforming triangle?

indicators.note: transforming means changing shape, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A mathematical value obtained by reshaping a triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: In calculus the area under a curve is computed as this value.

clue.text: Appalled observers taking in king — dressed in his new clothes?

indicators.note: taking in means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: shocked onlookers gape, so they are starers
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Shocked onlookers watching the emperor parade in his invisible outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts K inside STARERS. The emperor in the fable wore 'new clothes' that did not exist; starkers is British slang for naked.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fable the emperor's invisible outfit left him naked, which is the slang meaning here.

clue.text: Girl's clear about new feeling of congregation

parts.note: girl's as a possessive gives her

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: distinct means clear or easily perceived

explanation.surface: A girl's view of something fresh is unmistakable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N inside DISTINCT, making DINSTINCT. 'congregation' suggests church, but here it means any gathered crowd or flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency to follow the crowd is an urge shared by any flock or gathering.

clue.text: New poet's upset after one's dismissed as plagiarised?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are put in disorder
dismissed means removed, sent away from the word

parts.note: T. S. Eliot was a poet, and poet's gives his name with its s
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A fresh poet is furious after a rival is sacked for copying.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is T. S. Eliot; 'dismissed' drops the one, 'upset' shuffles the rest into ELOTS's new order, and N follows. The question mark admits plagiarism is theft only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagiarised work is taken from another without credit, effectively thieved.

clue.text: Source of colour and light encompassed in study

indicators.note: encompassed in means enclosed within the other word

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Colour and light filling a room set aside for study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompassed in' sets the light inside the study word. To con, meaning to study or learn by heart, is an old usage kept alive in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of coloured wax used for drawing gives colour to paper.

clue.text: Dubious venture ensnaring good writer

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping one thing inside another
dubious means doubtful or shady, telling us the letters are not in a reliable order

explanation.surface: A shady business scheme traps a decent author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' rearranges VENTURE into TURENEV, and 'ensnaring' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian novelist, author of Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Measuring device capturing oxygen in solar system body

indicators.note: capturing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: a meter is an instrument that measures, like a gas meter
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An instrument detecting oxygen inside a planet or moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts O inside METER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a piece of space rock burning up in the atmosphere, one of the objects orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Famous performer's debut falling a little short

indicators.note: falling a little short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a debut is a start, a first appearance

explanation.surface: A celebrity's first appearance disappoints slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling a little short' removes the last T from START.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity or leading actor is a big name.

clue.text: Sportsman's first to leave bed

indicators.note: first to leave tells us the opening letter departs from the word

parts.note: a player is a sportsman

explanation.surface: An athlete is the first to get out of bed in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to leave' removes the P from PLAYER. 'bed' means a stratum, as in a bed of rock, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological bed is a single stratum or seam of rock or soil.

clue.text: Look elsewhere for umpire?

explanation.surface: A cricket club seeks its match official from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The umpire is the one who gives batsmen out, so cryptically he is where an 'out' comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract work to an external supplier is to seek it outside; the official is the origin of dismissals in cricket.

clue.text: Devotee of healthier lifestyle, not weedy, say, but out of puff?

definitions.text: Devotee of healthier lifestyle, not weedy, say, but out of puff?

parts.words: Devotee of healthier lifestyle, not weedy, say, but out of puff?
parts.note: a person who shuns tobacco (weed) and never takes a puff; weedy and out of puff both pretend to describe a feeble, breathless fitness fan

explanation.surface: A health fanatic who is not scrawny yet still gets breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from cigarettes lives more healthily and never draws on tobacco.

clue.text: American island — in aleutians, I'll expect? Quite the reverse

indicators.note: quite the reverse tells us the run of letters must be read backwards
in tells us the letters sit inside the words aleutians, I'll expect

explanation.surface: A guess about whether an American island lies in the Aleutians, then a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SILLE sit in 'aleutianS I'LL Expect'; 'Quite the reverse' turns them round. Ellis Island in New York harbour was the immigration station.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island, in New York harbour, was the main US immigration station.
